correctness.rationale: At both faces the reward derivative of the displayed Lyapunov function cancels (x−x*)(a−a*) from its x derivative, leaving −(x−x*)(q(x)−q(x*)). The x term diverges at 0 and 1; the reward term diverges at the opposite face and is smooth on the included critical face. Thus the compact sublevel argument and largest-invariant-set test give convergence for every strict interior start. In the oriented system y>0 at finite times; z eventually becomes positive because it crosses z=0 only toward z>0, and remaining nonpositive prevents y→0. The exact ratio h=z/y solves a scalar linear tracking equation along the orbit with positive limiting damping F*q₁ and limiting forcing F*, so h→1/q₁ and 1/y∼Dt/q₁. Writing k=1/q₁, the quadratic graph coefficient m for z=ky+my² is fixed by −Dk²=F*(−q₁m−σq₂k²/2). The derivative of F cancels at this order. This coefficient is not merely formal: the ratio error h−k−my obeys a damped scalar equation with O(y²) forcing, hence is O(t⁻²) by exponential convolution. The reciprocal derivative is Dk+(Dm−Dk/L)y+O(y²); integrating once and reinserting y=(Dkt)⁻¹+O(log t/t²) gives the stated log coefficient and integrable remainder, hence finite C. No feedback-speed restriction is used. The log coefficient is allowed to vanish. value.rationale: Both endpoint equalities are intrinsic boundaries of the published equilibrium cases. Exact physical-time amplitudes for every interior start are useful near reward saturation, and the logarithmic correction detects feedback speed even though the leading laws cannot.
